title: discovery: the environment-scoped restriction-profile twin answers a constant open profile on hosts that register their own restriction profile (#35887)
body:
repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

Seam: spec:RestrictionProfileSchema → runtime:packages/rest/src/discovery-routes.ts (`registerDiscoveryEndpoints`)

**Defect: declared ≠ enforced.** PR #35887, the ADR-0138 D2 amendment, mounts an environment-scoped twin of the restriction-profile discovery route: `GET /api/v1/environments/:environmentId/discovery/restriction-profile`. On every host, for any id, it answers the framework's constant open profile: `allowCode: true` and every flow node type, `parallel_gateway`, `join_gateway` and `boundary_event` included.

A host that enforces a narrower profile (cloud's hosted kernel registers `RestrictionProfileEndpointPlugin` with `allowCode: false`, and its hosted restriction profile refuses those node types) therefore publishes, anonymously, facts that its own kernel does not honour.

**Measured.** Cloud pin round cloud#4920 at objectstack `16a96ac2bbde` probed the composed hosted host (the `apps/objectos` composition). It found:
- the unscoped `/api/v1/discovery/restriction-profile` still answers cloud's door;
- the twin answers `200` with the open profile, both for the real environment id and for `probe`.

Evidence: cloud dev report cloud#4920 comment 7070292704. The probe was a throwaway test and was not committed.

**Reach.** It is a public anonymous route. No reader reads the twin today: `os validate --target` reads the unscoped route. The first client that trusts it will author code or flow nodes that the environment then refuses. No access is gained, so this is not a security finding. It is the "declared ≠ enforced" class.

**Fix shape (proposal).** `registerDiscoveryEndpoints` serves the host's registered restriction profile on both the unscoped route and the twin whenever the host registers one, and the constant only when none is registered. That removes the route-order dependency between a host's door and the framework's mount. Add a test: a host that registers a narrower profile gets the same answer on both mounts.

Cloud records the twin in its anonymous-surface ledger as "framework constant, no data" (PR cloud#4921). It does not mount a cloud-side override, per the standing rule 「平台问题在平台修」.

Re-check: on a host that registers a restriction profile with `allowCode: false`, `GET /api/v1/environments/x/discovery/restriction-profile` still answers `allowCode: true` ⇒ the defect is present.
